newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court set to rule on controverial pay claim.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court set to rule on controverial pay claim.

text.p: Brazil's most senior court was expected to rule on Wednesday on a controversial pay issue which the government fears might undermine its drive to keep a tight grip on the federal payroll, an official said.

The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) was due to meet at 1400 local/1600 GMT and would probably rule on a case brought by 11 civil servants who claim they are entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise given to the armed forces in 1993, an STF spokeswoman said.

The civil servants cite a rule that entitles public sector workers to pay rises awarded to state employees in other categories. Government officials say a victory for the group might set a precedent for the entire federal workforce.
Newspapers have said an across-the-board pay rise of 28.9 percent could add $7.0 billion to the federal government's payroll spending which totalled about $42 billion in 1996.
